1	# CLAUDE.md
2	
3	Guidance for working in this repository.
4	
5	## Project
6	
7	Spring PetClinic REST, converted from Spring `@RestController` classes to
8	**OfficeFloor function injection**. Spring's DI, security, persistence and DTOs are
9	unchanged; only the request handling is now explicit function orchestration.
10	
11	<!-- https://officefloor.net/AGENTS.md -->
12	@AGENTS.md
13

1	## OfficeFloor REST endpoints
2	
3	Applies when adding or changing REST endpoints. This project serves REST through
4	OfficeFloor Function Injection, **not** Spring MVC controllers: each endpoint is a
5	pipeline of small function classes wired together in YAML.
6	
7	- Requires the OfficeFloor Spring Boot starter in the build:
8	  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter` (Spring Boot 4.x) or
9	  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-3-starter` (Spring Boot 3.x). Without it these YAML
10	  files are inert. (Rules below track these starter versions.)
11	- Define each endpoint as a YAML file under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/`,
12	  named `<path>.<METHOD>.yml` (e.g. `owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml` → `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`).
13	- One small function class per step; compose steps with `next:` and `outputs:`.
14	- Do NOT generate `@RestController`, `@GetMapping` or `@PostMapping`.
15	- Transactions: `govern: [ transaction ]` on steps, not `@Transactional`.
16	- Errors: a handler YAML in `officefloor/escalation/`, not `@ControllerAdvice`.
17	
18	### Worked example — `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`
19	
20	The whole shape of an endpoint. The sections after this one are the reference.
21	
22	`src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml`
23	
24	```yaml
25	# First step runs first. Validate before Load so an invalid body is a 400,
26	# not masked by a 404 for a missing owner.
27	validate:
28	  class: com.example.owner.ValidateOwner
29	  next: load
30	load:
31	  class: com.example.owner.LoadOwner
32	  next: apply
33	apply:
34	  class: com.example.owner.ApplyOwner
35	  govern: [ transaction ]
36	  next: save
37	save:
38	  class: com.example.owner.SaveOwner
39	  govern: [ transaction ]
40	  next: respond
41	respond:
42	  class: com.example.owner.RespondWithOwner
43	```
44	
45	```java
46	// One public method each. State moves by Out<T> (set) → @Val (read), matched by type.
47	public class ValidateOwner {
48	  public void validate(@RequestBody @Valid OwnerRequest request, Out<OwnerRequest> body) {
49	    body.set(request); // body read once here; republished for later steps
50	  }
51	}
52	public class LoadOwner {
53	  public void load(@PathVariable("ownerId") int ownerId, OwnerRepository repository,
54	      Out<Owner> ownerOut) throws OwnerNotFoundException {
55	    Owner owner = repository.findById(ownerId);
56	    if (owner == null) throw new OwnerNotFoundException(ownerId); // handled below
57	    ownerOut.set(owner);
58	  }
59	}
60	public class ApplyOwner { // @Val yields the stored object, not a copy — mutate in place
61	  public void apply(@Val OwnerRequest request, @Val Owner owner) {
62	    owner.setFirstName(request.firstName());
63	    owner.setLastName(request.lastName());
64	  }
65	}
66	public class SaveOwner {
67	  public void save(@Val Owner owner, OwnerRepository repository) {
68	    repository.save(owner);
69	  }
70	}
71	public class RespondWithOwner {
72	  public void respond(@Val Owner owner, ObjectResponse<OwnerResponse> response) {
73	    response.send(OwnerResponse.from(owner)); // this step responds; 200 by default
74	  }
75	}
76	```
77	
78	`src/main/resources/officefloor/escalation/com.example.owner.OwnerNotFoundException.yml`
79	
80	```yaml
81	handle:
82	  class: com.example.owner.HandleOwnerNotFound
83	```
84	
85	```java
86	public class HandleOwnerNotFound {
87	  public void handle(@Parameter OwnerNotFoundException ex,
88	      ObjectResponse<ResponseEntity<String>> response) {
89	    response.send(new ResponseEntity<>(ex.getMessage(), HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND));
90	  }
91	}
92	```
93	
94	### Step wiring
95	
96	Each top-level YAML entry is a developer-chosen step name; the first is the entry
97	point. `class:` names the function. **Give each function class exactly one public
98	method** — several public methods fail at start-up unless every reference adds
99	`method:`.
100	
101	- `next: <step>` — run that step afterwards. This step's return value arrives there
102	  as `@Parameter T`.
103	- `outputs: { <name>: <step> }` — conditional branches. Declare a
104	  `@FunctionalInterface` parameter annotated `@Flow("<name>")` and call it to take the
105	  branch; not calling it short-circuits.
106	
107	### Function parameters
108	
109	Declare only what the step needs; they resolve by role:
110	
111	- `@PathVariable`, `@RequestParam`, `@RequestBody` — Spring MVC annotations work.
112	- Spring beans (repositories, mappers, services) — injected by type as normal.
113	- `ObjectResponse<T>` (`net.officefloor.web.ObjectResponse`) — send the response with
114	  `response.send(dto)`. This is how a step responds; wrap as
115	  `ObjectResponse<ResponseEntity<T>>` to set status explicitly.
116	- `@Parameter T` (`net.officefloor.plugin.section.clazz.Parameter`) — the previous
117	  step's return value, a `@Flow` argument, or a thrown escalation.
118	
119	### Passing state between steps — `Out<T>` / `@Val`
120	
121	Steps do not call each other. Beyond the single `@Parameter` hand-off, publish state
122	into a variable (`net.officefloor.plugin.variable`):
123	
124	- Producer declares `Out<T>` and calls `set(...)`; consumer declares `@Val T`.
125	- Matching is **by type** — two variables of the same type in one pipeline need a
126	  `@Qualifier` annotation to disambiguate.
127	- `@Val` yields the same object the producer stored, **not a copy** — so an `Apply`
128	  step mutates the entity in place and later steps see the change.
129	
130	### Naming
131	
132	Verb plus entity: `Load<E>` (fetch by path variable, publishes `Out<E>`, throws when
133	absent) · `Build<E>` (construct from body) · `Validate<E>` (bind and validate the body,
134	publish it) · `Apply<E>` (mutate) · `Save<E>` · `Delete<E>` · `RespondWith<E>` (200) ·
135	`RespondWith<E>Created` (201) · `RespondWithNoContent` (204).
136	
137	Keep DTOs at the edges — request body in at the first step, response DTO out at the
138	responder. Steps in between work with entities.
139	
140	### Request body and validation
141	
142	- The HTTP body can be read only once: **only one step per pipeline may bind
143	  `@RequestBody`**. A second binding fails at runtime. When later steps need it, the
144	  first step publishes it as a variable.
145	- `@Valid` runs before that step's method body, so step order decides when validation
146	  happens. Put the validating step first — otherwise a missing id returns 404 before an
147	  invalid body can return 400.
148	
149	### Transactions
150	
151	`govern: [ transaction ]` for writes, `govern: [ readonly-transaction ]` for reads,
152	listed on **every** step it covers. Both are provided by the starter. Governance spans
153	the pipeline, so the request commits once at the end.
154	
155	### Errors
156	
157	Functions throw; handlers respond. The exception must be **checked** (`extends
158	Exception`) so it appears in the `throws` clause. Put the handler in
159	`officefloor/escalation/<fully.qualified.ExceptionClass>.yml`, taking the exception as
160	`@Parameter` and responding via `ObjectResponse`. Matching is most-specific-first;
161	anything unmatched falls through to Spring `@RestControllerAdvice`.
162	
163	### Security
164	
165	Guard a whole endpoint file with a Spring Security SpEL expression:
166	
167	```yaml
168	composition:
169	  authorize: "hasRole('OWNER_ADMIN')"
170	```

# Spring PetClinic REST - Owner implementation (for adding an optional `email` field)

## Architecture summary
REST is served through **OfficeFloor function injection**, not Spring MVC controllers. Each endpoint is a YAML pipeline under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/` wiring small single-method function classes. The request/response **DTOs are code-generated at build time** from an OpenAPI spec (`src/main/resources/openapi.yml`) by the `openapi-generator-maven-plugin` into package `org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.dto` (suffix `Dto`). MapStruct maps DTO↔entity. Entities carry JPA + jakarta validation annotations. **There are already three failing/target acceptance tests that require the `email` feature.**

Key insight: to add `email` you will edit (1) `openapi.yml` `OwnerFields` schema (the DTOs are generated, not hand-written — do NOT look for `OwnerFieldsDto.java` in `src/main`), (2) the `Owner` entity, (3) the SQL schema for the hsqldb profile used by tests, and add lowercasing logic in an Apply/Build or a new Normalize function.

---

## 1. Entity / model classes

**`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/model/Owner.java`** — `@Entity @Table(name="owners") extends Person`. Fields: `address` (`@NotEmpty`), `city` (`@NotEmpty`), `telephone` (`@NotEmpty @Digits(fraction=0,integer=10) @Pattern("^[0-9]{10}$")`), `pets`. Standard getters/setters and a `toString`. An `email` field would be added here with a `@Column(name="email")` and validation such as `@Email` (nullable, so no `@NotEmpty`).

**`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/model/Person.java`** — `@MappedSuperclass extends BaseEntity`. Fields `firstName`, `lastName` (both `@Column` + `@NotEmpty`).

**`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/model/BaseEntity.java`** — `@MappedSuperclass`, `Integer id` (`@Id @GeneratedValue(IDENTITY)`), `isNew()`.

---

## 2. Owner DTOs (generated — defined in OpenAPI, not Java source)

DTO classes referenced by functions: `OwnerDto`, `OwnerFieldsDto`, `OwnerPageDto`, all in package `org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.dto` and generated into `target/generated-sources/openapi/...`. Defined in:

**`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/resources/openapi.yml`**
- `OwnerFields` schema (lines ~1991-2041): the editable request body. Properties `firstName`, `lastName`, `address`, `city`, `telephone` — each with `type/minLength/maxLength/pattern/example`; `required: [firstName,lastName,address,city,telephone]`. **This is where you add an `email` property** (type: string, format: email, not in `required` so it's optional). The generator has `performBeanValidation=true`, so an OpenAPI `format: email` / `pattern` becomes jakarta validation on the generated DTO, enforced at the `ValidateOwner` step.
- `Owner` schema (lines ~2042+): `allOf` of `OwnerFields` plus read-only `id` and `pets`.

Generator config in **`/home/daniel/sandbox/pom.xml`** (lines ~369-411): `generatorName=spring`, `modelNameSuffix=Dto`, `modelPackage=org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.dto`, `interfaceOnly=true`, `performBeanValidation=true`, `useJakartaEe=true`, `serializationLibrary=jackson`.

Mapper: **`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/mapper/OwnerMapper.java`** — MapStruct `@Mapper(uses=PetMapper.class)`. Methods `toOwnerDto(Owner)`, `toOwner(OwnerDto)`, `toOwner(OwnerFieldsDto)` (ignores id, pets), `toOwnerDtoCollection`, `toOwnerPageDto`. MapStruct maps by matching property names, so an `email` on both entity and DTO is mapped automatically.

---

## 3. OfficeFloor Owner YAMLs (`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/`)

- **`owners.POST.yml`** (create) — pipeline: `validate` (ValidateOwner) → `normalize` (NormalizeOwnerTelephone) → `checkTelephoneUnique` (CheckOwnerTelephoneUnique) → `build` (BuildOwner) → `save` (SaveOwner) → `respond` (RespondWithOwnerCreated). Guarded by `authorize: "hasRole('OWNER_ADMIN')"`. Steps after validate use `govern: [ transaction ]`.
- **`owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml`** (update) — `validate` → `load` (LoadOwner) → `apply` (ApplyOwner) → `save` → `respond` (RespondWithOwnerUpdated). All `govern: [ transaction ]`.
- **`owners/{ownerId}.GET.yml`** — `load` → `respond` (RespondWithOwner), `readonly-transaction`.
- **`owners.GET.yml`** — single `service` step ListOwners, `readonly-transaction`.
- Also present: `owners/{ownerId}.DELETE.yml`, `owners/{ownerId}/pets.POST.yml`, `owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}.PUT.yml`, `owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}.GET.yml`, `owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits.POST.yml`, `v2/owners.GET.yml`.

Note the POST pipeline is where an email-lowercasing/normalize step would fit (mirroring `NormalizeOwnerTelephone`); the PUT pipeline uses `ApplyOwner` to copy fields.

---

## 4. Owner function classes (`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/function/owner/`)

- **`ValidateOwner.java`** — `@Validated`; `service(@Valid @RequestBody OwnerFieldsDto request, Out<OwnerFieldsDto> validated)` publishes the validated body. Validation of the DTO (including a future `@Email`) fires here.
- **`BuildOwner.java`** — `service(@Val OwnerFieldsDto request, OwnerMapper, Out<Owner> built)` → `ownerMapper.toOwner(request)`. (Used by POST.)
- **`ApplyOwner.java`** — `service(@Val Owner owner, @Val OwnerFieldsDto request)` copies address, city, firstName, lastName, telephone into the entity. (Used by PUT.) **You must add `owner.setEmail(request.getEmail())` here for PUT to persist email.**
- **`NormalizeOwnerTelephone.java`** — strips non-digits, requires 10 digits, throws `InvalidTelephoneException`. Static `toDigits(String)`. Good template for an email-lowercasing normalize step (create path). Note the create path does NOT reuse ApplyOwner, so email lowercasing on create should happen in a normalize step or in BuildOwner/via mapper.
- **`CheckOwnerTelephoneUnique.java`** — uniqueness check via `ownerRepository.findAll()`.
- **`LoadOwner.java`** — loads by `@PathVariable ownerId`, throws `NotFoundException`.
- **`SaveOwner.java`** — `ownerRepository.save(owner)`.
- **`RespondWithOwner.java`** — 200 with `OwnerDto`.
- **`RespondWithOwnerCreated.java`** — 201 Created with Location header.
- **`RespondWithOwnerUpdated.java`** — sends NO_CONTENT body with `OwnerDto`.
- **`ListOwners.java`** — list/filter by `lastName`.
- Others: `ListOwnersPage.java`, `BuildOwnersPet.java`, `LoadOwnersPet.java`, `DeleteOwner.java`.

Important for the "lowercase email" test: create (POST) goes ValidateOwner → NormalizeOwnerTelephone → CheckOwnerTelephoneUnique → **BuildOwner** (mapper) → SaveOwner. There's no ApplyOwner on create, so lowercasing must be added either as a new normalize function in `owners.POST.yml`, in `BuildOwner`, or in the mapper. For PUT, add `setEmail` to `ApplyOwner`.

---

## 5. Existing owner tests (already require the email feature)

**`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/test/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/acceptance/AcceptanceTest.java`** — 3 tests, all on `POST /api/owners` + `GET /api/owners/{id}`:
- `coreLowercasesEmail()` — posts `email="Test.User@Example.COM"`, expects `GET` to return `$.email == "test.user@example.com"` (email must be **stored lowercased**).
- `errorRejectsInvalidEmail()` — posts `email="not-an-email"`, expects **400 Bad Request**.
- `functionalityAcceptsMissingEmail()` — posts owner with no email, expects 2xx (email is **optional**).

**`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/test/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/acceptance/AcceptanceBase.java`** — base with `@SpringBootTest @AutoConfigureMockMvc @Transactional @WithMockUser(roles={"OWNER_ADMIN","VET_ADMIN","ADMIN"})`. `ownerNode()` builds a valid owner JSON (firstName, lastName, address, city, telephone — no email). Helpers: `createOwner`, `createOwnerOk`, `getOwner`, `uniqueEmail()` (returns `owner{n}@example.test`), `extractId`. Uses `tools.jackson` (Jackson 3) ObjectMapper.

These three tests define the exact acceptance criteria: optional, `@Email`-valid, stored lowercased, returned in the response DTO.

---

components:
  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type
          description: Full URL that originated the error response.
          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'
          readOnly: true
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The short error title.
          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time
          example: '2024-11-23T13:59:21.3820407Z'
          readOnly: true
        schemaValidationErrors:
          title: Schema validation errors
          description: Validation errors against the OpenAPI schema.
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationMessage'
      required:
        - type
        - title
        - status
        - detail
        - timestamp
        - schemaValidationErrors
    ValidationMessage:
      title: Validation message
      description: Messages describing a validation error.
      type: object
      properties:
        message:
          title: Message
          description: The validation message.
          type: string
          example: "[Path '/lastName'] Instance type (null) does not match any allowed primitive type (allowed: ['string'])"
          readOnly: true
      required:
        - message
      additionalProperties: true
    Specialty:
      title: Specialty
      description: Fields of specialty of vets.
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          title: ID
          description: The ID of the specialty.
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 0
          example: 1
          readOnly: true
        name:
          title: Name
          description: The name of the specialty.
          type: string
          maxLength: 80
          minLength: 1
          example: radiology
      required:
        - id

          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:

          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:

          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:

          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:

          type: string

          maxLength: 20
          example: '6085551023'
      required:
        - firstName

## Summary

I implemented the optional owner `email` field per the spec: present-and-invalid → 400, and stored/returned lower-cased. The implementation follows the project's OfficeFloor idiom, mirroring the existing telephone-normalization pattern.

**Changes:**

1. **`openapi.yml`** — Added an optional `email` property to the `OwnerFields` schema (not in `required`), so the generated `OwnerFieldsDto`/`OwnerDto` carry the field.

2. **`model/Owner.java`** — Added the `email` field with `@Column(name = "email")`, getter/setter, and `toString`. (Left off entity-level `@Email` deliberately, so Hibernate's on-save validation can't diverge from the normalizer and turn a 400 into a 500.)

3. **`NormalizeOwnerEmail.java`** (new) — Reads the validated request; if email is present it lower-cases it (`Locale.ROOT`), validates syntactic validity via regex, and either mutates the request in place or throws the checked `InvalidEmailException`. A null email is left untouched (optional).

4. **`InvalidEmailException` + `InvalidEmailExceptionHandler` + escalation YAML** (new) — Maps the exception to a 400 `ProblemDetail`, exactly mirroring the telephone handler.

5. **Pipelines** — Inserted `normalizeEmail` after `validate` in both `owners.POST.yml` and `owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml`. `ApplyOwner` (PUT path) now copies `email`; the POST path picks it up automatically via MapStruct (matching property names).

6. **Schemas** — Added a nullable `email` column to hsqldb, h2, mysql, and postgres `schema.sql`. Since the hsqldb seed used positional `INSERT ... VALUES`, I converted those owner inserts to an explicit column list so the added column doesn't break them.

**Design note:** validation lives in the normalizer (custom regex + checked exception → 400) rather than relying on a generator-emitted `@Email`, making the 400 behavior deterministic and independent of the OpenAPI generator's annotation output — and it also handles the lower-casing in the same single-responsibility step.
